title: Tenant-aware audit delivery: adaptive backpressure, dedup, and SIEM contracts
creator: Priya Shah
description: Implement a tenant-aware audit delivery subsystem that guarantees delivery semantics to external SIEM/webhook sinks (Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs API, generic webhooks) while minimizing duplicate events and maintaining observable SLOs. Work includes: defining an event envelope v2 (idempotency id, seq, tenant_id, schema_version, checksum), adding per-tenant backpressure and rate controls, durable buffering with ordered replay for tenants that require chronological guarantees, and a configurable deduplication window. Trade-offs: exact once requires cross-datastore consensus and large operational cost; we propose pragmatic at-least-once with strong idempotency and tenant-visible dedupe metrics as a balance. This ticket covers protocol design, runtime implementation, QA, and rollout strategy with canary and fallback paths.
acceptance_criteria: New event envelope v2 accepted by security and product (schema and migration plan documented)
Splunk HEC and Datadog adapters support idempotency header and retry semantics with observable metrics
Per-tenant backpressure can throttle/buffer without impacting other tenants (verified under load)
Deduplication reduces duplicates to <1% for normal retry storms (measured in staging)
Recovery path: after transient sink outage, ordered replay maintains per-tenant ordering for events with ordering requirement flag
Runbook updated and alerting created for audit forwarder DLQ and sequencing anomalies

decisions: Use envelope v2 with explicit event_id, tenant_id, seq (optional), schema_version, and checksum
Adopt at-least-once delivery with strong idempotency and configurable dedupe window instead of distributed exactly-once
Per-tenant buffering with quota and priority tiers; global protection so noisy tenant cannot starve others
DLQ semantics: persistent append-only DLQ with automatic backfill and manual reconcile tools
Adapters for Splunk HEC and Datadog Logs will expose idempotency headers and accept batched payloads; generic webhook sinks will receive X-Idempotency-Key header
